terms.label: Initiative
terms.definition: Taking useful action early to complete work, respond to difficulties or handle an unexpected situation.

terms.label: Be proactive
terms.definition: Notice a need and take an appropriate first step before a problem grows.
terms.example: Avery notices the queue sign has fallen before opening and checks where to secure it.
terms.nonExample: Avery waits until a customer complains.

terms.label: Improve work practices
terms.definition: Suggest a practical change that makes a repeated task safer, clearer or more efficient.
terms.example: Kai proposes labelled packing trays and asks the team to test the new routine.
terms.nonExample: Kai changes agreed prices without checking.

terms.label: Share opinions respectfully
terms.definition: Explain a useful idea or concern, listen to others and give a reason.
terms.example: Sam explains that the queue blocks the accessible entrance and suggests a clear route.
terms.nonExample: Sam insults the team and refuses to listen.

terms.label: Help fellow workers
terms.definition: Offer useful assistance while respecting roles, workload and safety.
terms.example: Avery offers to restock bags while a trained colleague handles the till.
terms.nonExample: Avery abandons an assigned safety check to take over the till.

terms.label: Seek more responsibility
terms.definition: Ask to learn or take on suitable duties with the training and authority needed.
terms.example: Kai asks to shadow the stock check before learning to do it independently.

terms.label: Empowerment
terms.definition: Having an appropriate voice and scope to act in your work.

terms.label: Recognition
terms.definition: Others noticing and acknowledging a useful contribution.

terms.label: Efficiency
terms.definition: Using time and resources well while maintaining safety and quality.

terms.label: Work opportunity
terms.definition: A possible chance for new duties, training or advancement; never a guaranteed promotion.

checks.prompt: An untrained worker spots a faulty powered machine. What should they do first?

options.text: Keep clear, warn others as appropriate and use the workplace reporting process.
Repair it immediately to prove initiative.
Ignore it until told what to do.

checks.feedback: Useful initiative respects safety, competence and authority. Reporting a risk is proactive action.
checks.retryHint: Initiative does not authorise unsafe tasks.

checks.prompt: A team tests labelled trays and reduces packing errors. Which conclusion is supported?

options.text: Less rework can save time and materials while protecting quality.

checks.feedback: Explain the mechanism: fewer errors can reduce rework and waste. Recognition or opportunities may follow, but are not guaranteed.
checks.retryHint: Choose the effect supported by the situation.

lessons.title: Step in with purpose
lessons.subtitle: Notice. Check. Act. Explain.
lessons.objective: Recognise useful initiative, choose a safe response and explain a workplace benefit.
successCriteria: Explain initiative in your own words.
Distinguish five behaviours using a reason.
Connect an action to a plausible benefit.
lessons.priorKnowledge: Recall someone noticing a useful job before being asked. What made it helpful?

model.context: Avery is preparing a fictional market stall. A loose queue marker narrows the entrance.
steps: I notice a problem before opening: people may struggle to enter.
I check the agreed layout and my role. I do not move safety equipment without authority.
I explain the concern and suggest a clearer position to the stall lead.
With permission, I move the marker and check the entrance is clear.
This is proactive action and respectful communication. A clearer entrance may help customers and reduce disruption.
model.nonExample: Moving every barrier without checking access and safety is action, but it is not sound initiative.

transfer.prompt: Choose a new workplace situation. Describe what you notice, a safe action within your role, the behaviour it shows, and a plausible workplace effect.
transfer.scaffold: I noticed __. I checked __. I would __. This shows __ because __. It could help by __.

rubric.criterion: Links a defensible behaviour to the action.
Explains a plausible causal workplace effect.

transfer.scoring: Teacher reviews each criterion: demonstrated, developing or not yet evidenced. No keyword scoring.

retrieval.prompt: Without reopening the cards, explain initiative, recall five behaviours and explain one benefit.
retrieval.timing: After application, then teacher-scheduled revisits in a later lesson and week. School pacing remains unconfirmed.
retrieval.mastery: Practice accuracy is a support signal, not proof of transfer or formal assessment.
